about: Design recipe ledger for all mockups. Newest entries FIRST. Before building any mockup: run `node ledger-check.js` (or read the last 10 entries) — any displayFont, paletteFamily, or loaderConcept used in the last 10 entries is OFF the table for the new build. After building: append the new entry in the same commit as the mockup. Backfilled entries (pre 2026-06-09) have null block codes because the data wasn't recorded at build time.

entries.trade: Plastering, all aspects, Birmingham and a 15 mile radius. Brief was one WhatsApp line from Patrick: contact Matt Aston, phone 07909 607506, Birmingham 15 mile radius, plastering, all aspects, photos promised but not sent so build it on stock. No trading name supplied; Patrick chose 'Matt Aston Plastering'. No logo, no email, no address, no reviews, no website, no accreditations.
entries.paletteFamily: GOES ON PINK, COMES OFF WHITE, the two states of a skimmed wall. BRIGHT WHITE page + set grey #edefee section ground (the colour multi-finish dries to) + BERRY #8c1d49 as the single working accent on white (CTAs, labels, 01-06 chips, card top-lines, the accent word, the wet coats in the loader and the hero band), #a52357 the fill and #ff6fa8 the light on dark. WET SKIM #17191b does PANEL duty (loader ground, the whole 390 fold, the mobile nav, the about panel, the CTA band, the footer). The berry IS the plaster: it goes on wet in the accent and comes off flat pale grey, which is the one colour story a plasterer actually has. Argued vs the window and vs the two recent plasterers: bk-trading took the literal pale multi-finish tint #dda393 and used it as a LIGHT FIELD under ink type, ansar-construction drove the same material the other way into FIRED CLAY #c2542b and carried a whole terracotta poster fold; this is neither, it is a deep cool berry with no orange or brown in it, used only as a working accent on white while black does every panel, and it is the only build in the window with a pink or magenta anywhere. No red (gmh toolbox #d81e28), no orange (hive #ec5a00, first4driveways #f4572f), no teal (atherton #0b5c66), no cobalt (oakmile), no sign blue (john-van), no copper (gk), no gold (waterhouse), no yellow (brian-fox), no coral (guest-tiling #f04a58), no clay, no green, no lime.
entries.loaderConcept: OFF THE HAWK (NEW, ld-offthehawk, added to loader-lab this session): the plasterer's actual move, loading off the hawk and laying the wall up, then trowelling it off flat. On wet-skim near-black a hawk and a pat of berry plaster sit at the bottom-left corner (0.08-0.16s), then a solid trowel tracks left to right four times across the bare wall, bottom course to top, and each pass leaves a full-width band of WET BERRY behind it (0.34-1.30s) so the wall is laid up in coats rather than filled in one go; the pat lifts off the hawk as it goes. One long final pass then runs across the middle and the whole face turns to FLAT SET behind the blade (1.32-1.82s), a raking sheen crosses the finished wall the way a plasterer shines a light along it to check for flatness (1.72s), and MATT ASTON PLASTERING / Flat walls, ready to paint lands ON the finished wall (1.86s). Solid shapes, transform and opacity only, no linework, no SVG stage. 2.15s body.lit, 2.4s JS teardown, 2.7s CSS-only ldGoneAuto fail-safe, 3.0s JS removal; reduced-motion shows the set wall and the brand. Hands off INTO the fold: the band under the hero on desktop and directly under the 390 CTAs lays the same three berry coats and takes the same trowel pass to set on body.lit, so the loader's last move and the first mobile screenful are one continuous wall. Distinct from Trowel Float and Plane Pass (a float smooths an already-rough surface, nothing is laid), Skim Set, Cure and Dry (a wet wall drying off in patches, no trowel), Three Coats and Build & Skim (a section or a blockwork wall built then skimmed), Scrim Skim, Tape Feather and Make Good (jointing and patching), Dot & Dab and Boards On (boards going up), Roller Sweep (paint) and Comb & Bed (adhesive ridges and tiles): nothing else in the lab loads off a hawk, lays a wall up in coats and then trowels the coats off to a set finish.

entries.loaderConcept: Herringbone Lay (NEW, ld-herringbone, added to loader-lab this session; replaced a first cut, Grid Green, which Patrick cut with "i dont like the loader, just doing some nice paving being put down"). Nice paving being put down, and nothing else. A dark screeded bed wipes in from the left (0.06-0.48s), then 88 solid blocks land on it one after another on a 0.015s beat (0.34-1.66s), each dropping 20px with a scale overshoot and a settle, laying LEFT TO RIGHT across the bay so there is always a ragged working edge exactly like a gang moving across a job. Weighted brindle mix, mostly reds with buff occasionally and charcoal rarely, sampled off their own photos. Their real alpha-keyed mark fades under the finished bay at 1.6s with 'Block paving, laid and jointed'. Transform and opacity only, no SVG, no linework. THE GEOMETRY IS REAL, which is why it reads: a true 90-degree herringbone (pair = one 2x1 flat block plus one 1x2 upright block) tiled on the lattice (3,1) and (-1,1), verified zero overlaps and zero gaps, then the whole field is rotated 45deg and cropped by the stage so it presents as the 45-degree herringbone a drive is actually laid in. Distinct from Whacker Pass, the other block-laying loader, which is the driveway trade's FINISH: kerb lines, a sand bed, three courses of stretcher bond and an orange compactor tracking over the lot. This has no kerbs, no compactor and no stretcher bond; it is the LAY itself in herringbone bond and the payoff is the finished pattern.

entries.flourish: The hero IS their own YouTube. All three of their videos are 720x1280 PORTRAIT phone reels, so the hero is a tall 9:16 reel panel rather than the full-bleed landscape video background the pattern library has always meant by 'hero video'. Autoplay, muted, looping a window that starts at 44s, the good bit. The trap worth recording: a PORTRAIT iframe makes YouTube serve the Shorts player, whose pause / prev / next glyphs and channel-name overlay ignore controls=0 and sat on top of the hero. The fix is to keep the iframe 16:9 (which gets the classic player, where controls=0 is honoured) and scale it by height until the pillarboxed portrait video covers the panel: aspect-ratio:16/9, height:104% on desktop, 178% at 390. pointer-events:none on the iframe so nothing can pause it, and the poster is held until the API reports PLAYING so no play glyph is ever seen either. Second flourish: the basketweave square from their own mark redrawn as a repeating SVG course behind the hero, every section and the CTA band.

entries.notes: REDESIGN, not a cold mockup: everything comes from their live site. FLAGS: (1) NO reviews exist anywhere for this business, so all three testimonials are PLACEHOLDERS. They are deliberately role-and-sector attributions (Site Manager, industrial development, Northamptonshire) with no invented personal names and no invented client company names, because this is B2B and a fake named individual at a fake named contractor is a worse fake-tell than a fake homeowner. Replace or remove before launch. (2) No accreditations claimed anywhere on their site, so none are shown. (3) 'Over 30 years' is their own claim, taken verbatim from their meta description and about copy, not inferred. (4) Nigel Mckie is only ever the company name on their site, never a public-facing person, so he is NOT named and CTAs say 'Call us' / the number. (5) Coverage chips are their own meta keywords list, which reads as a target list rather than a confirmed footprint; the H1 and headings say nationwide, which is their own wording. (6) Only a landline (01327 643328) is published, no mobile, so the FAB is CALL ONLY and there is no WhatsApp anywhere. (7) The LinkedIn URL in the footer is guessed from their 'Linkedin' link label, VERIFY it before launch; the YouTube channel URL is real (@NMLPaving-yo7hc). (8) Their 79 gallery photos include a handful with workers in them; the 18 used are the ones with no identifiable faces. (9) Hero video window is set by two constants at the top of the script, HERO_START 44 and HERO_END 88, judged off four sampled frames only, so the exact seconds are easy to retune.

entries.loaderConcept: Jobs Done (NEW, ld-jobsdone, added to loader-lab this session). Patrick's call on review: the first cut, Fix Run (a five-scene conveyor of little jobs each fixed as it landed), was 'a little bit confusing', and he asked for 'the checklist loader for items around the house that need doing'. On tool-steel black the label JOBS ROUND THE HOUSE fades up (0.04s) and five list rows stagger in on 0.10s (0.10-0.50s), each an empty rounded checkbox with the job beside it in Hubot 700 white: Dripping tap, Shelf up, TV on the wall, Wardrobe built, Hole in the wall. Then the list TICKS ITSELF OFF top to bottom on a 0.22s beat: the box fills toolbox red on a scale overshoot, a white tick pops in, and a red line strikes through the job left to right while the text dims to #9aa2ab (0.80-1.74s). A hairline rule draws under the finished list and GREATER MANCHESTER HANDYMAN / ALL DONE TODAY lands at 1.90s. Transform and opacity only, no SVG stage, no linework. 2.15s body.lit, 2.4s JS teardown, 2.62s CSS-only ldGoneAuto fail-safe, 2.9s JS removal; reduced-motion shows the fully ticked list and the brand. Hands off INTO the fold: the black band across the base of the hero is the same list carried on, a slow marquee of fourteen TICKED jobs (Dripping tap, Shelf up, TV on the wall, Wardrobe built, Hole in the wall, Light fitted, Door easing, Radiator swapped, Tiles regrouted, Lock changed, Kitchen tap, Fence panel, Loft hatch, Skirting on) on a red rail, so the loader's list and the first screenful are one continuous day's work. Distinct from ld-snaglist and ld-jobsheet, the two mono-era list cards in the lab that have never had a first use: both are a CONTRACTOR'S paperwork (a snag list on white, a paper job sheet on dark) written in monospace, which is now banned; this is the HOMEOWNER's own list in the brand's display face, and the tick-off is the animation rather than the sheet arriving. Distinct from Drive Home (hgm-property-services, the other handyman loader, which is one batten and two screws) and from A to Z, Four Day and Job Phases: nothing else in the lab ticks a list of household jobs off one by one.
entries.blocks: H-TODAY (NEW): two folds off one set of markup, joined by the jobs band. Desktop is a bright white split: eyebrow 'Salford . Greater Manchester', Hubot Sans 900 H1 'Same day handyman, plumbing and repairs across Greater Manchester' with Greater Manchester in toolbox red, lede, then a LIVE TODAY CHIP that reads the visitor's own clock (before 16:00 on a weekday 'Still taking same day jobs for today' with a pulsing green dot; 16:00-20:00 'Booking first thing tomorrow morning'; after 20:00 'Back on the phone from 7am'; Sundays 'Sundays by arrangement, give Ezekiel a ring'), always stamped with the real day and date, then red Call Ezekiel + ghost Get a Price (form link). Right is a 4:3.5 photo of a toolbox and drill stood at a customer's door with Ken Burns and an ink 'Out the same day' badge floating off its bottom-left corner. Under both columns a 96px BLACK JOBS BAND runs full bleed carrying the loader's ticked list on a 34s marquee with a red rail along its base. At 390 the WHOLE fold is a TOOLBOX RED POSTER: white knockout H1 with Greater Manchester in near-black, the today chip in a darkened well, white Call Ezekiel + outlined Get a Price two-up, then the photo below with the badge lifted out under it as its own ink card, then the black jobs band. Nothing else in the last ten has a red fold.+S2-PHOTO x8, every card photo-topped with an ink 01-08 chip top-left and a toolbox-red top-border sliding in from the left on hover (General Plumbing, Bathrooms & Showers, Electrics & Lighting, Painting & Decorating, Plastering & Skimming, Kitchen Fitting, TV & Appliances, Flat Pack & Repairs). One card per row at 390. Closed by CHIPS-REST (NEW): an 18-chip pill grid led by a black 'Also on the list' chip, carrying the rest of the 39 services they actually list on Gumtree, which turns their own long tail into content rather than binning it.+none (their portfolio photos are unusable). Replaced by P1, a three-step process (Ring or send the job / Price before we start / Out the same day), and an AREAS-GRID of 24 Greater Manchester towns with Salford as the black lead cell.
entries.flourish: The live today chip: the whole pitch on their Gumtree ad is SAME DAY, so the hero carries a chip driven by the visitor's own clock and date that says whether Ezekiel can still get out today. entries.loaderConcept: Whacker Pass (NEW, ld-whackerpass, added to loader-lab this session): the driveway trade's actual finish, the plate compactor pass. On logo black two kerb lines strike in top and bottom of a bay (0.06-0.56s), a sand bed fills between them (0.2-0.58s), three courses of solid brindle-grey blocks drop in staggered stretcher bond (0.42-1.24s), an orange whacker plate (solid plate, body, angled handle and grip, vibrating on a 0.08s loop) tracks left to right over the lot and exits (1.02-1.8s), then their own two swoosh curves (orange then white, stroke-dashoffset) sweep in low-left to high-right across the finished course (1.5-2.12s) and the real alpha-keyed logo lands under 'Laying the drive' (1.7s). 2.3s lit, 2.5s teardown, 3.0s fail-safe; reduced-motion drops the whacker and shows the finished bay and brand. Hands off INTO the hero: the drive band under the hero (desktop) and directly under the 390 CTAs rebuilds the same kerbs, sand, two block courses and whacker pass on body.lit, with the swoosh following, so the loader and the first screenful are one continuous job. Distinct from Comb & Bed (tiles into adhesive), Kerb Line (civils string line), flag-lay (slabs into a grid), surface course layup (cross-section fills), Laid to Falls and Road Open: nothing else in the lab lays block courses in bond and compacts them.

entries.seed:
SEED — First4Driveways, Colchester (CO3 3BZ)
Brief:     "do a mockup just improving on this one https://first4driveways.co.uk/ looks super AI".
           Branded REDESIGN. Their live site is an AI build: dark navy page, emoji service icons,
           zero photographs, stat tiles, "Essex & Wales" in the meta vs "Essex & Hertfordshire" in
           the body. Everything below keeps THEIR brand and replaces the AI tells with photos,
           a real hierarchy and motion.
Palette:   THEIR LOGO, BOTH COLOURS, IN THEIR ROLES. BRIGHT WHITE page + cool stone #eff1f3
           section ground + F4D ORANGE #f4572f (median-sampled off the FIRST4 letters in their own
           logo JPG, their theme-color is #e8450a) as the single working accent on white (CTAs,
           labels, card top-lines, accent word, call FAB), #d8430f the text-safe deepening.
           LOGO BLACK #111214 does PANEL duty exactly where their logo puts it: the loader ground,
           the whole 390 fold, the drive band under the hero, the about panel, the CTA band and
           the footer. The page is NOT dark: their site is dark everywhere and that is half of
           why it reads as AI. White does the work, black frames it.
Type:      Exo 2 800/900 display (the nearest Google face to the Eurostile-style wide squared sans
           of their FIRST4 DRIVEWAYS wordmark; x1 all-time in the ledger) + Inter 400/600 body
           (their live body font, kept).
Signature: THE DRIVE BAND. Their logo's swoosh is a road curve, so the page lays one. A full-bleed
           black band runs under the hero and on body.lit the loader's own block courses lay
           across it in stretcher bond, the orange plate compactor tracks over them and the
           logo's own orange-and-white swoosh sweeps along the finished course. Loader and hero
           are one continuous job.
Texture:   stretcher bond. Block courses in the loader and drive band; service card top-lines
           fill from the left like a course being laid; gallery tiles sit on a masonry grid.
Loader:    Whacker Pass (NEW, ld-whackerpass, to add to loader-lab): the driveway trade's actual
           finish. On logo black two kerb lines strike in, a sand bed fills between them, three
           courses of solid brindle blocks drop in staggered stretcher bond, an orange plate
           compactor (whacker) tracks left to right over the lot, then their own swoosh curves
           sweep in and the real logo lands. Caption "Laying the drive".
Voice:     no owner is named anywhere on their site, so CTAs are "Call us". Copy is homeowner-
           facing and short: what gets laid, where, on what guarantee.
Mobile:    the whole 390 fold goes LOGO BLACK and IS the logo: a large ghost version of their own
           orange+white swoosh sweeps in behind the white H1 on body.lit, then the drive band
           lays its courses and the whacker passes directly under the CTAs, all inside the 844
           fold. Photo drops below full bleed at 16:11 with the guarantee badge lifted out
           under it as its own black band.
Ledger ok: Exo 2 not in the last 10 (banned: Figtree, Chivo, Clash Display, Encode Sans Semi
           Expanded, Frank Ruhl Libre, Saira Extra Condensed, Titillium Web, Geist, Alexandria,
           Archivo Expanded). No black+orange-in-their-roles, no whacker loader, no
           H-DRIVEBAND+S2-PHOTO+G2 combo in the last 10.
Blocks:    hero:H-DRIVEBAND (new) / trust:T1 / services:S2-PHOTO x6 / about:slim ink /
           gallery:G2 masonry / reviews:R3 / areas chips / cta:ink band / contact:C1
entries.notes: BRANDED REDESIGN of first4driveways.co.uk, built on their system per the hard rule: live site rendered with Playwright at 1440 and 390 first (it is a Vite/React SPA, curl returns an empty root div), brand read off the rendered page: black page, #E8450A/#FF3C00 orange, Inter body, the only image on the whole site is logo.jpg. Logo is THEIR REAL MARK: logo-white.png is the black-background JPG alpha-keyed with nothing redrawn; logo-dark.png is the same file with the white DRIVEWAYS and swoosh recoloured to ink for the white nav. FLAGS: (1) Their site is almost certainly AI-generated end to end, so EVERY claim on it is suspect and was kept only where it is their own public statement: '15+ years', '10 year workmanship guarantee', 'fully insured', 'free quotes', the address 47 Butt Road CO3 3BZ, info@ email and the opening hours (from their schema). The '2,000+ projects', '500+ 5-star reviews', '98% satisfaction' and '991 Essex locations' stats were DROPPED as obvious AI filler. Confirm years, guarantee and insurance with the client before launch. (2) Their meta tags say 'Essex & Wales', their body copy says 'Essex & Hertfordshire'; the mockup follows the body copy. Confirm the coverage. (3) The six reviews on their site (Mark T., Sarah L., James R. ...) read as AI placeholders and were NOT reused; the four on the mockup are fresh PLACEHOLDERS and must be replaced with real Google/Checkatrade reviews at launch. (4) ALL photography is stock: six from the vetted stock-library groundwork-landscaping set (block-paving-driveway-fence, tarmac-drive-block-border, tarmac-driveway-new-build, grey-porcelain-patio, porcelain-patio-fence, sandstone-sett-patio, sleeper-steps-raised-beds, new-build-fencing-planting) and six from Pexels (37042905 curved setts hero, 15260092 resin texture, 29025379 gated gravel drive, 38220910 circular patio, 36779943 grey block path, 17366769 herringbone close-up, 38188641 contemporary patio), all checked for no people and no US tells; one US-looking house (12127809, porch columns and shutters) was pulled after review. They have no work photos on their site at all. (5) No owner is named anywhere, CTAs are 'Call us'. (6) No accreditations claimed (Marshalls Register, Interlay etc not on their site). (7) Some stock-library shots are small (612-760px) and sit in cards only.

entries.trade: NOT A TRADE. Commercial waste management, recycling, clearance and commercial vehicle hire, Peterborough head office (1 Milnyard Square, PE2 6GX) plus eleven other UK locations. Branded REDESIGN of hiveservices.co.uk. Brief was specifically to build a one-click skip ordering feature modelled on the 4A Trades order wizard.
entries.paletteFamily: THEIR BRAND AS THEY USE IT. BRIGHT WHITE page + their own cool stone #f1f1f1 section ground + HIVE ORANGE #ec5a00, pixel-sampled off their live site, doing BOTH duties they already give it: the single working accent on white (CTAs, labels, card top-lines, hex bullets, call FAB) AND a full-bleed FIELD on the location marquee band under the hero and on the CTA band, because orange full-bleed strips are already their motif. HIVE INK #1a1919 does PANEL duty exactly where they use black: the rounded nav pill, the loader ground, the whole 390 mobile fold, the about panel, the stats band, the footer. Their four division colours stay in their four roles and nowhere else (Waste amber #ffb21a, Recycling green #37b34a, Clearance teal #00a69c, Vehicle Hire blue #36abe1), used only in the loader's sorting bays. Argued vs the last 10: ansar-construction #c2542b and gk-plumbing-heating #b9662f are muted clay and copper browns, guest-tiling #f04a58 is a coral red, ijc #824c32 is chestnut, waterhouse #d8a41c and brian-fox #ffcd11 are gold and plant yellow, john-van #0c3f95 is sign blue, needed-services #00a238 is a true green, scrapkings #17d99b is bright mint and atherton #0b5c66 is petrol teal. #ec5a00 is a saturated true orange at ~23deg used as a FIELD, and it is the client's own registered brand colour, which the branded-redesign rule makes non-negotiable.
entries.loaderConcept: HEX CLOSE (NEW, ld-hexclose, added to loader-lab this session): mixed waste going out sorted, and their own mark assembling out of the sort. On Hive ink an orange conveyor bar strikes in across the stage (0.06-0.50s), then four solid waste blocks in dirty greys and browns run along it left to right and each drops off the belt into its own colour-coded hexagonal bay below (0.30-1.44s). The four bays, one per division, slide together and lock into a single orange hexagon (1.44-1.92s), a white tick drops into it as the counter of their own mark (1.90s) and the wordmark lands under it with 'Sorted' below (1.98s). Solid shapes, transform and opacity only, no linework. 2.05s body.lit, 2.3s JS teardown, 2.55s CSS-only ldGoneAuto fail-safe, 2.85s JS removal; reduced-motion shows the assembled hexagon, the tick and the brand. Hands off INTO the fold: the same orange belt runs full bleed along the bottom edge of the hero as the locations marquee, and the four division colours carry on into the service system. Distinct from Load Out (a pile goes into a tipper), Blade Clear (a dozer pushes a site clear), Skip Lift (a skip built and hoisted on a crane hook), Crush & Grade and Tipper Pour: nothing else in the lab SORTS a stream into colour-coded bays and builds the logo out of them.
entries.blocks: H-WIZARD (NEW): the hero's right-hand slot is not a photo, it is a WORKING skip order wizard. Desktop is a bright white split: eyebrow 'Peterborough and eleven other UK locations', Figtree 800 H1 'Skip hire, commercial waste and recycling, ordered in three taps' with 'ordered in three taps' in Hive orange, lede, orange Call + ghost Get a Quote (form link); right is a white card in an ink header, 'Order a skip / Three taps, no phone call needed', with three hexagonal step pips. Step 1 is four size tiles (4yd Mini / 6yd Midi / 8yd Builders / 12yd Maxi), each with capacity in bin bags and a to-scale orange skip silhouette (trapezoid body plus top rail) that fills orange on selection; step 2 is a postcode box and a three-way delivery-day chip row; step 3 is a summary with the guide price, and 'Book this skip' writes the whole order into the enquiry textarea and scrolls to the contact form with the name field focused (the H-PLATE precedent). A 74px full-bleed ORANGE conveyor band runs under both columns carrying the twelve UK locations as a marquee, straight out of the loader's belt. At 390 the WHOLE fold goes HIVE INK and IS the picker: eyebrow, three-line white H1 with the orange accent line, lede, then the wizard card, all landing at 813px inside the 844 fold, with the Call + Get a Quote buttons two-up directly under it. Nothing in the last ten has a working tool as the hero.+S2-HEX x9, every card photo-topped with a HEXAGONAL ink number chip 01-09 bottom-left of the photo (chip hidden at 390 so nothing sits inside a photo on mobile): Skip Hire, Collections & Bin Hire, Commercial Recycling, IT WEEE & White Goods, Confidential Shredding, Hazardous & Clinical, Construction Waste, Clearances, Commercial Vehicle Hire. Orange top-border slides in from the left on hover. One card per row at 390.+none (a waste management company has no work photos and their live site carries none). Replaced by P-SKIP, a four-step process with hexagonal step numerals (Pick and confirm / We check and deliver / Fill it at your pace / One tap, we collect), their own six 'Why Hive' points as a 3x2 hex-bulleted grid, an ink STAT4 band carrying their own numbers (85+ / 120+ / 95% / 50) and a 12-tile areas directory.
entries.flourish: THE HEX. Their mark is the V of 'Hive' caught inside a hexagon, so the hexagon is the whole geometry: section labels take a hex bullet, service card numbers are hex chips, the wizard's three step pips are hexes, the process numerals are hexes, the review avatars are hexes and the contact icon tiles are hexes. One motif, used everywhere, lifted straight off their logo rather than invented. Counted with the loader as the build's one signature move.

(4) Phone 0330 111 0080 is a non-geographic landline, so there is NO WhatsApp FAB, call-only. (5) 'Registered waste carrier' is claimed on the basis of the Waste Carriers Licence link in their own footer; the licence number itself was not published and is not claimed. entries.trade: Full home renovations and complete property refurbishments. Manchester based, projects running in Derby. Team of 7, works with housing associations, developers, landlords and homeowners, buys and renovates older properties itself, electricians within the team.
entries.paletteFamily: COOL BRAND, WARM PRODUCT. BRIGHT WHITE page + cool stone #f2f4f6 section ground + SITE INK #16181b at PANEL duty (loader ground, the whole 390 mobile fold, the about panel, the CTA band, the footer, the hero badge) + PETROL TEAL #0b5c66 as the single working accent on white (CTAs, labels, card top-lines, programme bar, call FAB; #3fbcc9 is the light version on the ink field and the wipe seam). The accent is deliberately COOL so the one warm thing on the page is the finished room itself: the lamplight #ffdcaf in the transformation illustration and the warm dusk kitchen photography. Argued vs the last 10: ansar-construction #c2542b and gk-plumbing-heating #b9662f are both warm clay/copper oranges (an orange accent was designed first and dropped on those grounds), waterhouse #d8a41c and brian-fox #ffcd11 are gold and plant yellow, guest-tiling #f04a58 is a coral red, ijc #824c32 is chestnut, john-van #0c3f95 is a saturated signage blue, needed-services #00a238 is a true green and scrapkings #17d99b is a bright light mint. #0b5c66 is a dark, desaturated blue-green at ~185deg used flat against ink and white, and it is the only cool-accent-plus-warm-photography pairing in the window.
entries.loaderConcept: Strip & Finish (NEW, ld-stripfinish, to add to loader-lab): the whole renovation in one room. On ink a tired room stands (stained ceiling, bare pendant, damp band along the wall, dark old units, worn boards, black window); the fittings fly out and the pendant with them and the damp fades (0.30-0.55s), the wall goes bare and the floor down to subfloor (0.44-0.55s), four studs rise (0.60-0.84s), a steel slides in under the ceiling with a settle (0.86s), three first-fix runs draw DOWN the wall (1.04-1.20s), four plasterboard sheets drop on (1.24-1.42s), then the FINISHED room wipes in left to right behind a cyan seam (1.48-2.0s) with the window lighting warm and three downlights on, and ATHERTON CONSTRUCTION SOLUTIONS / Managed from start to finish lands at 1.86s. Solid shapes, transform and opacity only, no linework. 2.15s body.lit, 2.4s JS teardown, 2.9s JS fail-safe; reduced-motion shows the finished lit room and the brand. Hands off INTO the fold: the identical room sits in the 390 ink fold and runs the same left-to-right wipe on an 8s loop with the same seam, and body.lit fills the five-segment programme strip under it. Distinct from Build & Skim (a blockwork wall built then skimmed), Property Run (the OUTSIDE of a unit built, washed and painted), Roof to Room (a gable elevation built top-down), Stud & Board (one partition), Room Set (a finished room being furnished), Knock Through (one wall opened and propped), Open Up (bifolds folding away) and Programme Chart (a gantt chart): nothing else in the lab strips a room back to its shell and rebuilds it through the trades.

entries.flourish: THE TRANSFORMATION: one CSS room built from solid shapes that wipes tired-to-finished behind a cyan seam, run three times (the loader sequence, the 390 mobile fold on an 8s loop, and the programme section). entries.notes: NOT A NEW-BUSINESS BRIEF but treated as one: the brief says they have an existing website and an Instagram, neither URL was supplied and no UK web presence resolves for the exact name, so on Patrick's instruction (2026-08-27) this was built ALL-STOCK. Flags for the client conversation: NO logo (ACS ink tile wordmark created from scratch), NO email, NO address, NO real reviews (all four are PLACEHOLDERS), NO real photography (every image is from the vetted stock-library: gen-builder, electricians, joinery, plumbing, decorators, bricklaying). Damien is NOT named anywhere on the page (not publicly front-and-centre). The brief's flagship 'before & after transformations' feature is delivered as the DRAWN transformation room, not as photo pairs, because honest matched before/after pairs are impossible with stock. No accreditations, insurance or years-trading claimed anywhere. Areas beyond Manchester and Derby are assumed from 'wider travel radius to be confirmed' and the copy says so. The brief also asks for ~25 SEO service and location pages: that is production-site scope, the mockup is the usual single page.

entries.loaderConcept: Lift In (NEW, ld-liftin, added to loader-lab this session): the developer's move rather than the tradesman's, a house is not laid, it is SET. On ink a cobalt footing bar strikes in along the base (0.08-0.52s), a hoist line drops from the top of the frame (0.25-0.55s) and whole STOREY SLABS come down the line and seat onto the stack one after another with a settle overshoot, ground floor then first floor (0.40-1.44s), the roof pitch caps the stack (1.30-1.82s) and OAKMILE lands on the finished house (1.56s). Solid shapes only, no linework, transform and opacity only, 2.15s teardown with a 2.6s fail-safe. Hands off INTO the 390 fold: body.lit rebuilds the same footing, storeys and roof as a ghost cobalt outline behind the H1. Distinct from Ground Up (roots below a ground line then blockwork rising course by course), Coursework (bricks only), Frame Raise and Truss Raise (timber structure standing up), Strata Rise (ground MADE in layers) and Topping Out: nothing else in the lab lifts finished floor plates in on a hoist and stacks them.
entries.flourishes: the storey line (a 2px cobalt datum rule with a square node, set at floor level, running under the H1 and every section label and along the about panel) + floor-plate banding (thin rules stacked at storey intervals across the ink about panel and CTA band)
entries.mobileMove: the whole 390 fold goes INK and IS the plot: the loader hands straight off into the hero, the storey stack it just built stays on screen as a ghost cobalt outline behind the knockout H1 and finishes building there (footing, ground, first, roof, staggered on body.lit), with Shepperton in cobalt, the storey line under it, and Call Dave + Discuss Your Project on the black.

entries.trade: Plumbing and general internal renovations. Patrick's call after seeing the photos: drop HEATING from the name and the positioning, and drop the outside work (fencing, garden clearance) entirely, it should not be featured. What is left is what the photos actually show: bathrooms and wet rooms taken back to the joists, first fix copper between the joists, cloakrooms and separate WCs, large format porcelain tiling and flooring, and full internal renovations including basic electrical work. Owner George Katakalos, trading as GK since 2020, 25 years on the tools. Harringay / South Tottenham N15, North London. Brief was a WhatsApp text summary plus 29 of his own photos (letterboxed 736x1600, cropped to 736x983); the 4 fence and garden photos were cut from the folder.
entries.paletteFamily: SLATE AND COPPER, THE TWO THINGS UNDER HIS FLOORS. BRIGHT WHITE page + cool stone #eef0f1 section ground + SLATE #182229, sampled off the grout-and-shadow grey that dominates his own marble-effect shower room photos (#82837b, #d0d2d1) and driven down, doing PANEL duty (loader, the whole 390 fold, the about panel, the CTA band, footer #0f171c) + COPPER #b9662f, pixel-sampled off the pipe runs in his lifted-floor photos, as the single working accent on white (#9c4d1c for small text, #e08b52 for accent words and labels on the slate, #8a4a22 for the second cold run). Argued vs the last 10, which has two warm browns in it: ansar-construction's fired clay #8f3f21 is a WARM FIELD carrying the whole 390 fold with white type on it, and ijc's #824c32 is their own logo brown on a white consultancy page. Here the field is COOL, a blue-cast slate, and the warm colour is a hot metal accent on top of it, so the fold reads cold-and-hot rather than all-warm. Deliberately NOT the plumbing trade-default blue: john-van-sales-commercials is running sign blue #0c3f95 and local-london-plumbers logo cyan #1ea4dd in the same window. No green, lime, violet, pink, yellow or gold anywhere.
entries.loaderConcept: Shower Reveal (NEW, ld-showerreveal, added to loader-lab this session). Patrick asked for it by name after the first concept was cut: "we actually do want a loader but just not the one we had ... just do a shower turning on and revealing his company name or soemthign". On slate a copper riser and a wide copper head drop in from the top with a settle (0.08-0.66s), thirteen pale water jets fall from the face one after another over 400ms and then run continuously on a soft shimmer loop, a pool of light blooms on the floor where the water lands (1.12s), four droplets pop off it, and the wordmark RISES up out of the pool (1.28s). Teardown 2.35s, fail-safe display:none at 2.95s. Solid shapes only, transform and opacity, no linework. The FIRST cut for this build was Board Over (ld-boardover): joists, a copper first-fix run, boards sliding over it. Patrick rejected that one along with the matching hero floor strip; its card is still in loader-lab with no first-use site, so do not treat it as proven. Shower Reveal is deliberately the same trade image as the older Shower On (ld-showerhead, jjs-services) built the other way round: there chrome fittings drop water ONTO a wordmark already sitting there, here the head is in the brand accent and the water REVEALS the name, which rises out of the splash. Second time Patrick has asked for exactly this image for a bathroom fitter, which is the standing lesson: the obvious literal picture beats the clever one.

entries.loaderConcept: Blade Clear (NEW, ld-bladeclear, added to loader-lab this session): site clearance as one move. On black, seven dark rubble blocks stand up along a dirt strip (0.05-0.55s), a solid plant-yellow dozer tracks in from the left with its blade down (0.4-1.55s) and every block ahead of the blade is shoved right and tips off the edge one after another (0.62-1.66s), leaving a clean yellow ground line behind the blade; the white wordmark lands on the cleared ground (1.6s). Solid shapes, transform and opacity only, no linework. 2.0s body.lit, 2.25s JS teardown, 2.5s CSS-only ldGoneAuto fail-safe, 2.8s JS fail-safe; reduced-motion shows the cleared strip, the parked dozer and the brand. Hands off INTO the fold: body.lit runs the identical dozer along the black ground band at the base of the 390 yellow poster and clears the same rubble, so the loader and the first mobile screenful are one continuous move. Distinct from Dig Out (an excavator scoops ground blocks away), Load Out (a pile goes into a tipper), Cut & Fill (teeth settle to a datum, no machine), Plant Out (three machines park and a headcount ticks) and Kerb Line: nothing else in the lab pushes a site clear with a blade.

entries.trade: Wall and floor tiling contractor, Stourbridge (DY8 5LL), Black Country and Worcestershire. Brief was a Facebook page scrape plus one line from Patrick that resets the whole positioning: 'It would need to be aimed more at national housebuilders. We do the odd domestic project but mainly it's contracting for the big boys.' So the site is written contract-facing (plots, house types, site programme, handover) even though all ten supplied photos are domestic jobs. Real logo (alpha-keyed off a white JPG, plus a knockout white version for the slate panels), real phone and email, no reviews at all, no address beyond the postcode, no accreditations claimed. Argued vs the last 10, which has two warm-red neighbours and this is neither: ansar's FIRED CLAY #8f3f21 / #c2542b is a warm orange-brown used as a FIELD carrying white type, the colour of wet plaster; adjudicate's #b73d2c is a warm brick red used as the DOMINANT hue on white with blush pink and deep teal and no dark panel anywhere. This is a COOL coral-crimson used strictly as an accent and a datum mark on a slate field, and it is the client's own printed logo colour, which is the strongest justification available. entries.loaderConcept: Comb & Bed (NEW, ld-combbed, added to loader-lab this session): the tiler's actual sequence, spread, set, grout. On slate a notched trowel sweeps left to right across the substrate and leaves eight solid adhesive comb ridges behind it (0.06-0.62s), then thirteen porcelain tiles bed into it one after another in HALF BOND, three courses with the middle one offset half a tile and running off both edges (0.46-1.22s), each with a settle overshoot. Grouting is one move, not many: a white ground wipes left to right BEHIND the tiles (1.24-1.56s) so every joint on the face fills at once, the way you actually grout a wall. The logo's red diamond then pops on a joint crossing as the datum (1.52s) and the knockout wordmark lands (1.58s). Solid shapes, transform and opacity only, no linework. 2.2s body.lit, 2.45s JS teardown, 2.6s CSS-only ldGoneAuto fail-safe, 2.9s JS fail-safe; reduced-motion shows the grouted wall, the datum and the brand. Hands off INTO the fold: body.lit strikes the same setting-out lines across the base of the 390 slate fold and beds the same half-bond course along it, left to right, with the same red datum landing last on a crossing. Distinct from Bed & Lay (a trowel spreads mortar and bricks drop, no comb ridges and no grouting), Tile Lay and Tile Set (tiles pop into a grid with no adhesive and no grout), Score & Snap (one tile being cut), Grout Sweep (grout alone on an already-tiled wall) and Herringbone Lay (block paving): nothing else in the lab combs a bed, lays to a bond and then grouts the whole face in one wipe.
entries.flourishes: 1. The Comb & Bed loader. 2. The setting-out band: a full-bleed slate grout-line grid running under the hero into the trust strip, with the logo's own red diamond as the datum mark where two lines cross. The same half-bond logic then sets the gallery, so the trade's own geometry is the page's structure rather than a decoration.

On graphite a hi-vis string line strikes across (0.08-0.53s, the way the job actually starts), then eight precast kerb units drop onto it one after another with a settle overshoot (0.44-1.77s), each seating against the line with a chamfered top face, then concrete haunching wipes in behind the finished course (1.42-1.87s) and the wordmark lands above (1.6s). 2.0s body.lit, 2.25s JS teardown, 2.5s CSS-only ldGoneAuto fail-safe, 2.8s JS fail-safe; transform and opacity only; reduced-motion shows the finished haunched course and the brand. entries.trade: bricklaying, Sheffield. Brief from Patrick 2026-08-26 was the Instagram bio line ('Sheffield based bricklayers with 40+ years of experience and knowledge. DM for a free quote') plus 8 Instagram screenshots of their own work (extension blockwork, porch, gable over new roof, engineering-brick gable, facing brick off scaffold, new-build footings, long garden wall) and a 150px logo thumbnail. NO phone, email, address or reviews supplied: Wren pattern consts empty, call CTAs fall to #contact, WhatsApp FAB and email/Instagram cards hidden until wired, 4 placeholder reviews (Hillsborough, Dronfield, Rotherham, Chapeltown). 40+ years is their own claim and is used; no insurance or accreditation claims. Repointing card uses the vetted stock-library shot; every other photo is theirs. Photos are low-res IG screenshots (480-666px): ask for originals.
entries.microFont: none (DM Sans 600 small-caps labels, .74rem); Cinzel 700 ONLY for the wordmark lockup
entries.paletteFamily: THEIR OWN WALLS. BRIGHT WHITE page + BLOCK GREY stone #eceef0 section ground (the grey of their concrete blockwork) + FIRED SHEFFIELD RED #a2361c doing FIELD duty (the whole 390 poster fold, the about panel, the CTA band, the footer #7d2914) with a drawn stretcher-bond mortar-joint SVG pattern over every red field so each panel reads as a brick wall; #8f2f18 text-safe accent on white, #c9552f as the lit brick face. Ink #1b1c1f from the logo for type. NO black, grey or navy panel anywhere: the only panel colour is the brick. Argued vs the last 10, every one of which is a separate hot ACCENT riding an ink/anthracite/brand PANEL (traffic red on hot-rolled plate, arc blue on gunmetal, cedar+tan, silage green+gold, tape yellow, steel blue+coral, claret, forge orange on iron black, J&L blue, slate blue): this is a single-hue system where the brick red IS the field and the accent is the same hue, the first red FIELD in the ledger. RC's #d0181f (same day) is a blue-cast RAL signal red used as a small accent on white over a grey plate; this is an orange-cast fired clay used as whole panels with no plate. Their photos are wall-to-wall this brick, so terracotta is the material, not a mood.
entries.hero: H-BRICKFOLD (NEW): two genuinely different folds off one set of markup, both built around THE FORTY, a giant DM Serif Display '40' ghost numeral. Desktop is a split: copy left on white (pulsing-dot eyebrow 'Sheffield bricklayers . 40+ years' experience', keyword H1 'Bricklaying, Extensions & Garden Walls in Sheffield' with Sheffield in brick red, the ghost 40 at 7% brick behind it, then the live COURSE RULE: five mini bricks that drop in one by one on the loader hand-off, lede, Call us + Get a Free Quote) against their own sunlit long-wall photo right in a 16px frame with a '40+ years / Laying brick in and around Sheffield' badge in-photo DESKTOP ONLY. At 390 the fold flips to a full-bleed FIRED RED BRICK WALL poster: the stretcher-bond mortar pattern over the whole panel, the ghost 40 in white at 12% top right, white serif H1 with Sheffield underlined, the course rule in white, both full-width CTAs (white fill + white outline) landing at 603px inside the 844 fold, photo below on white with the badge lifted out as its own card.
entries.loaderConcept: Bed & Lay (NEW, ld-bedlay, added to loader-lab this session): the bricklayer's actual action rather than a wall appearing. On white a steel trowel (solid blade, stem and ink handle) travels left to right along the footing spreading a grey mortar bed behind it (0.08-0.8s), six fired-red bricks with a lit top face drop onto the bed one after another with a settle overshoot (0.58-1.72s), then the vector-traced roofline mark + Cinzel wordmark + 'Sheffield . 40+ years' land above the finished course (1.55s). Solid shapes only, no linework. 2.2s JS teardown, 2.8s removal, CSS-only ldGoneAuto fail-safe at 2.5s, transform/opacity only, reduced-motion shows the finished course and brand. Hands off INTO the hero: body.lit lays the five-brick H1 course rule at both viewports. Distinct from Coursework/Cap It Off (courses appear in half-bond, no tool), Toothing Key, Make Good, Harl Cast, String Line and Ground to DPC: nothing else in the lab shows the trowel and the bed.

BRIGHT WHITE page + COOL TILE GREY #edf0f2 section ground, the grey porcelain that runs through every one of his bathroom photographs, + CEDAR DECK #5b3a1e doing PANEL duty (loader ground, the 390 poster fold, the about panel, the CTA band #40270f, the footer) with TIMBER TAN #8a4f1c as the single working accent on white (#6f3f16 text-safe deepening, #e8c9a4 as the light timber face on cedar). Argued vs the last 10: the window is harvest gold + silage green, tape yellow + ink, steel blue + coral, front-door claret, forge orange on black, J&L blue, slate ink + wet slate blue, board ink + chartered violet, plaster orange, and marble + resin teal. Nothing anywhere in the window is BROWN in any duty, and every entry in it is the same shape, a near-black or hot-hued INK PANEL carrying a separate hot ACCENT. This is a SINGLE-HUE system: the panel is the brand colour and the accent is the same timber hue at a different value, so the page is only ever two materials, cool grey tile and warm cedar board, which is literally what his portfolio is made of. The cool stone is deliberately cool against the warm brand colour rather than drifting to the banned warm paper.
entries.hero: H-BOARDRULE (NEW): two genuinely different folds off one set of markup, both built around THE BOARD RULE, a reeded cedar batten with fine decking grooves. Desktop is a split, copy left on white (pulsing-dot eyebrow Pontypool . 40 mile radius, keyword-led H1 'Kitchens, Bathrooms & Building Work in Pontypool' with the town in timber tan, then the BOARD RULE drawing itself out to 352px under the H1 on the loader hand-off with a warm light glide travelling it on a 7s cycle, lede carrying his own scope line, Call us + Get a Quote) against his best photograph full height right in a 16px frame, a raised deck with a stainless and glass balustrade over the wooded Torfaen valley, with a Free quotes badge in-photo DESKTOP ONLY, lifted out below the image as its own bordered card at 390. At 390 the fold flips to a full-bleed CEDAR POSTER: the copy block goes cedar edge to edge, ghost deck-board grooves fade in behind the stacked white H1 on body.lit, the board rule redraws in light timber, and a DRAWN GLASS BALUSTRADE rises along the bottom edge of the copy (steel rail scaling out, four glass panels fading in, five posts standing up in sequence, on a reeded light deck edge), continuing the loader straight into the page. Both full-width CTAs land at 618px and the balustrade bottoms out at 730px, inside the 844 fold. H1 bottom at 269px. The real photo lands below the fold on white so no text ever sits inside a photograph at either viewport.
entries.loaderConcept: Deck & Glass (NEW, ld-deckglass, added to loader-lab this session): the outdoor money shot built in front of you. On cedar six deck boards lay in left to right one at a time (scaleX from the left, so each runs out like a real board), the balustrade posts rise off the finished deck in sequence, the glass panels fade in between them under a steel top rail, and a hillside settles up behind the glass so the closing beat is the VIEW the balustrade was fitted for; CK BUILDING and Pontypool . South Wales land above it. Distinct from Deck Lay (ld-deck), which only lays boards and stops, and from Fence Line, which drops opaque timber panels between posts with nothing to see through. Solid shapes throughout, no outline strokes. 2.0s body.lit, 2.2s JS teardown, 2.8s removal, CSS-only ldGoneAuto fail-safe at 2.5s, transform and opacity only, reduced-motion shows the finished deck and the brand. Hands off INTO the fold: body.lit draws the board rule at both viewports and stands the 390 fold's glass balustrade up on its deck edge.

entries.loaderConcept: Lights On (NEW, ld-lightson, added to loader-lab this session). Third execution: two earlier versions were cut on review. v1 drew a house in thin line and SLID the facade off to the left, which read as a glitch. v2 kept the linework but peeled the facade with a warm cut line to reveal the house in architectural SECTION, and Patrick killed it (2026-08-25, 'the loader just doesn't make any sense really'): a cutaway section is an architect's device, not a builder's, and thin diagrammatic linework takes too long to parse in two seconds. The fix was to stop drawing a DIAGRAM and start showing the TRADE, in SOLID SHAPES rather than outline strokes. v3 is the build sequence: on claret a GROUND line strikes across (0.38s), the WALLS rise off it on a slight overshoot (0.5s at 0.22s), the ROOF drops on from above and settles (0.4s at 0.66s), door and window openings go in (1.02s), then the LIGHTS COME ON room by room, downstairs first then upstairs (1.14s, 1.27s, 1.40s, 1.53s), so the closing beat is somebody living in the finished house. Wordmark 1.48s, 2.45s teardown with a 3.2s fail-safe, transform and opacity only. Slate roof #4a4147, cream walls #f4ece4, accent front door #a8283f and warm #ffd9a8 window light: reads as a house instantly at 390px. It argues start-to-finish AND does the INSIDE half of the inside-and-out proposition through the lit windows, with no cutaway needed. The same lit house is reused as the About panel motif, so loader, about art and the door-mark favicon are one family.

entries.loaderConcept: Spray Pass (NEW, ld-spraypass, added to loader-lab this session): the only loader in the lab that atomises paint rather than dragging it. On Nelson navy a bare chalk wall stands in a hairline frame (0.08s), an airless gun on an extension pole enters top left with its FAN CONE open (0.22s), and it travels left-right, right-left, left-right laying three vermilion bands (0.34 / 0.76 / 1.16s) that each overlap the last by half with feathered leading edges, exactly how a sprayer works a wall. The payoff is the FLAT OFF beat: the visible seams between passes crossfade to nothing (0.82 / 1.2s) and the flat face resolves at 1.56s so three bands become one perfectly even surface, because a sprayer is judged on one thing only, whether you can still see where the passes were. Steps MASKED / SPRAYED / FLATTED OFF land on their own beats in tracked sans (no mono anywhere), then the GM wordmark rises on the fresh wall at 1.66s over PAINTING AND DECORATING . NELSON. 2.2s JS teardown + 2.8s removal + CSS-only ldGoneAuto failsafe at 2.5s, reduced-motion static finished wall + brand. Hands off INTO the fold: body.lit on the teardown beat draws the vermilion rule under the H1 and draws the navy cut-in line down the desktop fold. Deliberately does NOT re-run the trick in the fold, which holds a finished two-colour wall instead (the jm-builders / root-to-roof / project-colour same-trick-twice cut). Distinct from every decorating piece in the lab, all of which drag or lay a coat with a tool in contact with the wall: Roller Sweep rolls two bands under an illustrated roller with sleeve and grip on bare plaster, Second Coat wipes three hard-edged full-screen coats off a travelling roller bar, Brush On and Panel and Paint work a brush, Three Coats builds up successive plaster coats, Trowel Float and Skim Cure work a float. Nothing anywhere in the lab has a spray gun or a fan cone, nothing overlaps passes, and nothing makes SEAMS DISAPPEARING the payoff
entries.flourish: Two only: the Spray Pass loader, and THE CUT-IN as a running motif (the hero join drawing down on load, a 3px masked-edge tape line in the adjacent colour along every section top, and the service chip bars growing left to right on hover). Every colour change on the page is a hard line, never a fade

The red is ONE FLAT HUE with ONE JOB: the datum hairline, the section rules and the CTA fills. It is never a surface, never a fill between cells, and it is never split into facet tints.
           Argued vs the sister build (rws-contracts, same logo, same red): that page is a white ground with GALVANISED STONE cards and the mark's three fold planes broken out as light/mid/shadow tints laid down as 2px red compartment WALLS between grid cells. This page has no compartment system at all: the working surface is board grey at full-section scale, the red is a single 1px datum line, and the only ink is a photographic poster ground. Signature: BOARD BECOMES FINISHED. Drylining is the only trade whose whole job is to disappear: the board goes up grey with visible taped joints and screw dimples, and the finished interior is what the client actually buys. So every photograph on the page ARRIVES the same way it does on site: it enters board grey and desaturated behind a soft skim veil, and a diagonal SKIM SWEEP passes across it once and takes it to full colour. Gallery tiles, service rows and the hero panel all do it. It is a treatment of one photograph, never a before/after claim about one room.
Texture:   the datum. A single red hairline with setting-out ticks runs the width of the fold, and every section divider is the same hairline rather than a grey rule. Services are not cards and not a grid: six full-width BOARD COURSES, stacked rows, photo left, big Host Grotesk numeral, one-line description, the datum rule growing across the row on hover.
Mobile:    THE SKIM WIPE FOLD. The first 390px screenful is a full-bleed ink poster carrying their portrait corridor shot. It starts flat board grey behind a skim veil, and as the loader tears down a soft diagonal sweep passes across it and the whole fold resolves into the finished teal and white interior, once, slowly, with the red datum line drawing along under the stacked three-line H1. Slow Ken Burns underneath. No captions or badges sit inside the photo at 390.
Loader:    Tape and Joint (NEW, ld-tapejoint, added to loader-lab this session): on ink, two board sheets slide in and butt up leaving a visible tapered joint, a row of screw dimples pops in, the red datum snaps across, then a jointing blade sweeps down the joint and the joint and dimples fill and vanish into one flat plane, and the RWS mark lands on it. Under 2.5s, transform/opacity only, reduced-motion safe.

entries.loaderConcept: Daylighting (NEW, ld-daylight, added to loader-lab this session): the trade argued in one shot. On below-ground ink a suction NOZZLE and its corrugated hose drop in from above and hover a few inches over a tarmac-capped ground band (0.12-0.62s), a column of spoil particles STREAMS UP off the ground into the nozzle mouth under a drifting dust haze (0.55-1.4s), the ground band splits and slides apart to open a VOID beneath it (0.52-1.5s), and lying in that void, untouched, a yellow GAS main, a blue WATER pipe and a red ELECTRIC duct draw themselves in one after another (1.02 / 1.16 / 1.30s), because the whole product is that the soil left and the services did not. Ticks LOCATED / EXPOSED / INTACT in tracked sans (no mono anywhere), then their real alpha-keyed logo, recoloured to a light face for the ink ground, rises at 1.54s over VACUUM EXCAVATION . STROOD, KENT . UK WIDE. 2.2s JS teardown + 2.8s removal + CSS-only ldGoneAuto failsafe at 2.5s, reduced-motion static void-with-services + brand. Hands off INTO the fold: body.lit on the teardown beat draws the orange rule under the H1 at both viewports. Deliberately does NOT re-run the trick in the fold: the loader EXCAVATES (spoil rises, void opens, services revealed), the 390 poster instead runs a LOCATOR SCAN over services already at rest, so it is a survey rather than a dig (the jm-builders / root-to-roof / project-colour same-trick-twice cut). Distinct from every ground loader in the lab, all of which move earth with a blade or a bucket or build ground up in layers: Dig Out scoops ground blocks away, Trench Dig sweeps a bucket through strata, Trench Cut opens a trench behind a blade, Formation cuts a surfacing box and compacts it, Strata Rise makes ground in layers, Pile Drive hammers a pile down. Nothing anywhere in the lab removes material by AIR, nothing has a suction nozzle or a rising particle column, and nothing reveals a buried utility and holds it as the payoff

entries.loaderConcept: Delta T (NEW, ld-deltat, added to loader-lab this session): a commissioning readout rather than a build. Plant box and emitter box fade in at either end, the FLOW leg draws left to right in heat red while its mono readout counts UP 20 to 70 degrees, the RETURN leg draws back right to left in the logo blue while its readout counts DOWN to 50, and the payoff is the DELTA-T 20 degree chip popping dead centre between the two legs, because a system is not finished when it is running, it is finished when the difference across it is right. Mono ticks FLOW / RETURN / BALANCED; the real alpha-keyed badge rises at 1.5s over mono PLUMBING . HEATING . AIR CONDITIONING . DUBLIN. 2.3s JS teardown + 3.0s removal + CSS-only ldGoneAuto failsafe at 2.6s, reduced-motion static readout + brand. Deliberately does NOT hand off into the hero: the mobile fold runs a different move (the delta mark + wave sweep, no temperatures anywhere) to avoid the same-trick-twice cut taken on jm-builders, root-to-roof and project-colour. Distinct from every thermal loader in the lab: Ignition draws a pipe and lights a flame, Hot Meets Cold brings hot and cold pipes to a mixer tap, Pressure Test sweeps a gauge to 1.5 bar, Rad Bleed keys a radiator and warms the fins, Deep Freeze plunges one readout to -18, Split-Unit Breeze tilts a louvre and ticks one temperature down, Heat Bounce reflects heat off a coated wall. None run a circuit with two legs and none show a DIFFERENCE between two figures.

entries.loaderConcept: Seal the Line (NEW concept, added to loader-lab as ld-sealline): on white, a slate pitch draws in ink (0.12s), four slate courses draw across it parallel to the eaves in sequence (0.34-0.62s), lead flashing dresses into a chimney abutment on the right slope with a settle overshoot (0.98s), then the payoff: a continuous GREEN SEAL BEAD runs the whole junction ridge-to-eaves in one pass (1.24s) and RAIN starts falling and sheets straight off the pitch into the gutter on loop (1.5s), because a sealed roof is one where the water only ever goes one way. Mono ticks SLATED / FLASHED / SEALED / WATER OFF; Darker Grotesque RoofSeal wordmark + mono sub ROOFING . LEADWORK . GUTTERING rise at 1.7s. 2.2s JS teardown + 2.8s removal + CSS-only ldGoneAuto failsafe at 2.5s, reduced-motion static. Hands off INTO the fold: body.lit on the teardown beat draws the green rule under the H1 accent phrase at both viewports, and the fold's own slate-and-gutter run keeps raining on loop. Distinct from every loader in the window (three plain logo rises, a brand rise, a bar rise, a logo-sketch wipe, post-and-rail with strained wire, rafters up with a rooflight, shutter-and-pour with a laser, strata rise): nothing in the window or the lab rains, and nothing seals. Roofing-family cousins both differ: ld-slaterun (in the lab, unused here) only CASCADES slates down a pitch with no lead and no water; ld-dronesurvey (ag-roofline, cut on review) flies a drone over a roofline and scans it. This one bunds the joints and then proves them with weather. SAME-DAY NOTE vs mcs-maintains (parallel session, landed in the ledger while this was being built): their Lights On lifts three gable outlines on a MIDNIGHT page and lights the windows cyan, the payoff being a house lit and dry again; this draws ONE roof on WHITE and its payoff is water, a green bead sealing the junction and rain sheeting off into the gutter. Opposite polarity, opposite time of day, and nothing of theirs rains. REVIEW EDIT (Patrick 2026-08-18, 'the thing on the top of roof peak, remove, not sure what that is'): the bedded ridge tile at the apex was cut and the RIDGED tick became SLATED, so the sequence is now pitch, courses, lead, seal bead, rain, and the apex is a clean point

Argued vs the two black-and-gold builds that landed the SAME DAY: paul-marchant-lead-roofing is a full-dark lead-graphite #101214 ground with TORCH GOLD #e3aa32 (~42deg, a flame, a light-source register) and jbc-homes-developments is a full-dark midnight ink #0e1016 with ANTIQUE BRASS #c39a5e (~36deg at ~57% lightness, a desaturated heirloom metal). This build inverts both on the axis that matters most: the PAGE IS WHITE and the dark never carries the fold on desktop, the accent is ~31deg at ~40% lightness and full chroma, and it is a MATERIAL-TIMBER register, pine and chipboard, not a metal or a flame (the gilt-vs-machine-yellow same-family-different-register precedent applied across ~5-11deg of hue plus a value drop). Argued vs ollerton-plant-civils, the window's other warm accent: drain orange #dd5c14 sits ~21deg at high chroma on a stone POSTER page with no dark panel anywhere; pine honey is 10deg gold-side, darker, and this build does run a dark panel. No timber/honey accent on a white page anywhere in the window. Blues/greens/teals/reds/navies untouched. Story: the page is the new board, the dark is the loft before he gets there, and the honey is the pine ladder he leaves in it
entries.loaderConcept: Ladder Drop (NEW concept, added to loader-lab as ld-ladderdrop): the ceiling line draws across, the hatch unlatches and swings down on its hinge, a three section timber ladder telescopes out of the opening one section at a time and the feet land on the floor line, warm light spills down through the hole, and the JMCF wordmark rises up out of the hatch. Hands off INTO the hero: the loader teardown adds .lit and the hero batten strikes on the same beat, so the light continues rather than vanishing (gilfillan handoff precedent). 2.35s, transform/opacity only, fail-safe teardown at 3.2s, reduced-motion drops the ladder and shows the brand card

Argued vs jbc-homes-developments, which landed the SAME DAY from a concurrent session on the same written instruction (the ollerton/ashlea same-day-same-brief precedent, diverged deliberately on every shared axis once the collision was found): jbc is a NAVY-SIDE midnight ink #0e1016 logo-lift ground carrying CREAM #f0e9db headings and a desaturated ANTIQUE-BRASS gold #c39a5e (~36deg, ~57% lightness, a logo's rule metal at heirloom register) with champagne #e9d5a9, and its gold never floods a surface; this build is a COLD-NEUTRAL graphite ground (zero hue cast, the trade's own metal) carrying PURE WHITE headings and a hotter, higher-chroma FLAME gold #e3aa32 (~42deg at ~54% lightness and roughly double the chroma, a light-source register not a metal-object one: the gilt-vs-machine-yellow precedent applied inside one hue family), plus an achromatic milled-lead prop rail jbc has no equivalent of, and the one full-gold flood at cta duty. vs the rest of the window: the only other gold is knights-flooring's pale satin champagne on a WHITE page (opposite ground), and the only other full-dark is fraser-hoehle's green-charcoal + neon LED green (opposite accent family and register). jacobs-crown (warm ink + saturated crown gilt) stays aged out. entries.loaderConcept: Lead Burn v2, dome raise & burn (NEW concept, added to loader-lab as ld-leadburn; v1, a flat two-sheet seam weld, was CUT on Patrick's review 2026-08-14 as 'not ambitious enough' and replaced same session): on near-black, a gold line draws the OGEE DOME ELEVATION (the profile of the client's own bell dome in the hero photo, 0.08-0.58s), the base line and four curved wood-roll ribs draw in lead grey (0.45-1.1s), the dome FILLS with a milled-lead gradient (0.78s), then the payoff: a torch flame climbs the centre seam bottom-to-top (SMIL animateMotion, 1.0-1.8s) welding it in a glowing gold line, and the FINIAL SPHERE pops gold on the apex with an overshoot at 1.82s, because dressing a dome and burning its seams IS the specialism the whole brief hangs on; mono status ticks SHEET CUT / DRESSED TO ROLL / SEAM BURNED / FINIAL SET, then the Marcellus 'Paul Marchant' wordmark + mono 'Specialist Lead Roofing' sub rise at 1.8s. 2.3s JS teardown + 2.9s removal + CSS-only ldGoneAuto failsafe at 2.6s, reduced-motion static welded dome + brand. Hands off INTO the fold BOTH viewports: on mobile the drawn dome resolves into the REAL dome photo carrying the full-bleed fold beneath it (the drawing becomes the photograph), and the H1's gold weld-rule under 'lead' draws at 2.05s on the same register. Distinct from every loader in the window (a house elevation builds in construction order, colour chips fan and flood, a video fold, drains lay and run, ground rebuilds in strata, cages tie and pour, survey stations set, steel connections detail and stamp, heat bounces, mirrors demist) and argued vs the same-day jbc ld-elevation, the nearest neighbour (also gold line-art drawing a building): jbc draws a WHOLE HOUSE front-on in construction order and lights its windows, a builder's sequence ending in handover; this draws ONE ROOF FORM in section, fills it with the trade's own metal, runs a FLAME up it and caps it with a finial, a metalworker's sequence ending in a weld, and nothing anywhere else WELDS or BURNS. vs the lab's roofing set: Slate Run cascades slates down a pitch, Rain Shed sheds rain, Re-roof strips and re-tiles; nothing draws a dome and nothing torches a seam

entries.loaderConcept: Run & Fall (NEW concept, added to loader-lab as ld-runfall): on sub-base stone, a drainage run gets LAID and then RUNS. Two inspection chambers rise out of the ground with an overshoot settle (0.18s and 0.34s), a drain-orange run draws itself between them at a visible FALL (0.62s), pea-gravel bedding settles under it in an eight-step stagger (1.06-1.41s), a dashed datum line and a mono FALL 1:80 marker snap on at 1.34s to show the drop, and then the payoff: water starts flowing down the run from the high chamber to the low one on an infinite loop from 1.5s, because a drain that falls the right way IS the job. Mono status ticks CHAMBERS SET / RUN LAID / BEDDED & HAUNCHED / FALL CHECKED / CONNECTED, then the Sofia Sans OLLERTON wordmark + mono 'Plant & Civils . Wigan' sub rise at 1.72s. 2.2s JS teardown + 2.8s removal + CSS-only ldGoneAuto failsafe at 2.6s, reduced-motion static laid-and-running drain + brand. Hands off INTO the fold BOTH viewports: the hero closes on a bordered GROUND PANEL carrying the same run, chambers, bedding and dashed datum, tagged in mono 'FOUL RUN . 150MM . FALL 1:80', its pipe drawing at 2.05s and its flow starting at 3.2s, so the loader does not vanish, it parks in the page; at 390px that panel sits directly under the CTAs and the programme rail and is fully inside the first screenful, and the H1's orange rule grows at 2.05s on the same register. Distinct from ashlea-developments' Formation, landed the same day in the same trade: that loader DIGS A SECTION AND REBUILDS IT IN STRATA (a vertical cross-section, turf/subsoil/membrane/sub-base/blacktop, geology, what the ground is made of); this one lays a single horizontal run between two objects and puts WATER through it, which is hydraulics, not geology. Distinct from the rest of the window and the lab (cages get tied and poured over, survey stations set, steel connections detailed and stamped, heat bounces off a wall, mirrors demist, floors lay, staircases build, hedges trim, fences build) and from the lab's near neighbours: Dig Out SCOOPS ground blocks away, Trench Cut opens a trench along a marking line, Jet Clear blasts sludge out of a pipe that ALREADY EXISTS. Nothing anywhere LAYS A DRAIN, and nothing CHECKS A FALL

entries.loaderConcept: Shower On (NEW, added to loader-lab as ld-showerhead): on dark navy, a chrome riser and rainfall shower head fade down into place, then sixteen pale-blue #8fd8f5 water streams fall from the head in staggered infinite loops and land ON the JJS SERVICES wordmark sitting beneath, with a soft blue pool of light blooming behind the brand where the water hits; ~1.7s to settled, 2.2s teardown + 2.5s JS failsafe, reduced-motion hides the rig and shows the brand card. PATRICK SPECIFIED THIS DIRECTLY at review: 'i dont really get the loading screen, just do a shower head with blue water coming out on to the JJS Services name'. STANDING LESSON RECORDED: this mockup burned two cleverer loaders before landing. v1 'Step Down' (bath cross-section whose near wall dropped away while a dimension counted 520mm to 40mm) was cut as 'not a major fan of the animated climbing over the bath thing'; v2 'Panel Up' (four wall panels sliding up, yellow trims drawing down the seams) was cut as 'i dont really get the loading screen'. Both were conceptually defensible and neither read at a glance. For bathroom and shower fitters the OBVIOUS LITERAL IMAGE beats the smart one: a shower, running, over the name. Panel Up is kept in loader-lab as a valid concept for panel fitters, but note the read-at-a-glance failure before reaching for it. Water is otherwise unused in the lab, the earlier DPS hot-fill attempt having been cut; this is falling rain from a fixed head rather than a filling vessel

entries.archetype: C (photo-led premium, ink-panel hero on a bright page)
entries.palette: BRIGHT WHITE page + cool stone #f2f3f5 + GRAPHITE SLAT INK #14171c panels (hero, about card, cta band, footer; the exact charcoal of the client's own acoustic slat wall, the only two photos he sent) + OAK TAN #a9622a single working accent at SETTING-OUT-PENCIL / RAW-TIMBER register (~26deg, ~42% lightness, medium chroma: CTAs, FAB, nav CTA, form button, svc top-border slide-ins, trust ticks, review stars, eyebrow dot, section-label bars, the gauge line struck across every slat field, and the offcut that gets scribed off the last board; #8c4f21 hover) with a pale timber highlight #f0c48a carrying the scribe line itself. Argued vs the three warm accents in the 10-window: hgm's SITE ORANGE #ee5b1f is a full-chroma PPE/site orange at 54% lightness doing hazard-register duty on an ink drawing-board page; jm-builders' SATIN BRASS #8f6c22 is a dull low-chroma METAL at ironmongery register sampled off cabinet handles; this is neither hazard nor metal, it is the colour of the bare timber edge and the carpenter's pencil line, sampled off the raw ply return and the exposed batten in his own two photos, and it appears as a physical PIECE OF WOOD in the art (the offcut) rather than as livery. Dark-panel trigger fires on the photography: the product he actually sells is a charcoal slat wall, so the ink is his material, not a mood.
entries.loaderConcept: Slat & Scribe (NEW carpentry concept, added to loader-lab as ld-slatscribe): on white, a black felt backing field, then fourteen slats rise from the floor line in staggered sequence AT GAUGE with a settle (0.18-1.26s), a pale timber SETTING-OUT LINE strikes across the whole field at 0.9s, and then the payoff, the thing that actually makes the trade: the last board lands OVERSIZE (1.0s), the scribe line strikes down it (1.3s) and the OAK OFFCUT shears away and drops out of frame (1.55-2.23s) leaving the board sitting tight, because the last board on any wall never fits and always gets scribed. Mono ticks BACKED / SET OUT / SCRIBED; Rethink Sans NEBRO CARPENTRY wordmark + mono sub CARPENTRY . BIRMINGHAM . 30 MILES rise at 2.0s. 2.45s JS teardown (fired off a requestAnimationFrame so the render-blocking font link cannot eat the animation) + 3.05s removal + CSS-only ldGoneAuto failsafe at 2.75s, reduced-motion static field + brand. Hands off INTO the fold: body.lit on the teardown beat draws the oak rule under the H1, and the hero IS the same drawing continued at BOTH viewports, a live slat field whose gauge tick travels and whose last board re-scribes on an 8s loop. Distinct from every carpentry loader in the lab, which all work on a single piece of stock or a single opening (ld-doorsetout sets a door out in PLAN and counts a dimension, ld-mitreclose closes a casing corner, ld-dovetail slides a joint, ld-sawcut and ld-kerf cut across stock, ld-setout strikes lines on a board, ld-stud and ld-partition build studwork, ld-stairbuild builds a flight): nothing anywhere clads a WALL, and nothing takes waste off a board to make it fit. Argued vs the window's Battened Out (roof-tech, battens landing at gauge across a membrane): that is a ROOF PITCH, horizontal, and its payoff is a gutter and a downpipe carrying water away; this is a vertical interior wall and its payoff is a piece of waste timber coming off.
entries.blocks: hero:H-SLATFIELD (NEW variant: the hero IS a built slat wall. A graphite slat field of 30 boards fills the whole hero at both viewports, rising in sequence on load straight out of the loader, an oak gauge line struck across the top with a tick travelling it, and one board mid-field re-scribing itself on an 8s loop. Desktop puts the H1 on the field left with his own cropped slat-wall photo in a 16px frame right and a floating Slat & Panelled Walls badge in-photo DESKTOP ONLY, lifted out below the CTAs as its own full-width card at 880. entries.hero: H-CUTLINE (NEW): two genuinely different folds off one motif, the sculpted topiary profile that is the most distinctive thing they own (their roadside conifer run on a red brick wall, in two of their nine photographs). Desktop is a split, copy left on white (eyebrow Leeds . Gardens, Grounds & Fencing, keyword-led H1 'Garden Maintenance, Hedge Cutting & Fencing in Leeds' with the city in fresh green, lede carrying their own review language of turning up on the agreed day and taking every bit of waste, Call + Get a Quote) against their own topiary-and-brick-wall photograph full height right in a 16px frame, with the 'Free quotes / All waste taken away' badge in-photo DESKTOP ONLY, lifted out below the photo as its own bordered card at 390. Between the H1 and the lede at both viewports sits the signature CUT LINE: a sculpted hedge profile (three domes into a level run) filled at 17% with a fresh-green stroke that DRAWS ITSELF along the top edge on the loader hand-off (body.lit) and redraws on a 7s cycle, over a hairline rule and the caption 'Cut back, shaped, waste taken away'. At 390 the fold flips to a full-bleed HEDGE-INK POSTER: the hero ground goes #14201b, the H1 stacks white with Leeds in green, and a large topiary silhouette rises 26px and fades in from the bottom of the copy column on the hand-off with the SAME accent stroke drawing along its crown, so the loader's cut, the hero cut line and the poster crown are one idea in three places. H1 bottom lands at 244px and both full-width CTAs at 630px inside the 844 fold; the photo tucks straight under the silhouette with the badge lifted out below it.

entries.loaderConcept: Topiary Pass (NEW, ld-topiary, added to loader-lab this session). On hedge ink a dashed string line strikes across, a sculpted hedge fades in already carrying sixteen shaggy uprights, and a white trimmer bar with teeth travels the run left to right shaving the uprights to nothing in sequence while clippings fall away, revealing three sculpted domes into a level run underneath. A red brick wall course lands beneath it, ticks CUT BACK / SHAPED / CLEARED AWAY, and the alpha-keyed logo-light lockup sets over 'Gardens, Grounds & Fencing . Leeds'. Distinct from the lab's existing Hedge Cut, which trims a FLAT hedge face and is the only other hedge loader there: this one does not level a hedge, it SCULPTS one, and the shape it arrives at is the exact profile of the client's own roadside topiary run. Nothing else in the lab shapes a form rather than levelling, laying or assembling one. 2.2s JS teardown + 2.8s removal + CSS-only ldGoneAuto failsafe at 2.5s, reduced-motion shows the finished sculpted hedge and the brand. Hands off INTO the fold: body.lit draws the hero cut line at both viewports and raises the 390 poster silhouette with the same accent stroke drawing along its crown.
entries.flourishes: THE CUT LINE (one idea, three places: the loader's shave, the drawn hero rule under the H1, the poster silhouette crown at 390). Logo alpha-keyed out of its pale green gradient JPEG by modelling the background with an iterated max-filter and dividing, giving a clean transparent mark on white plus a recoloured light version for the ink panels, rather than redrawing it.
